correctness.rationale: A factor containing a pair of adjacent ones with gap g has outer runs L,R with L+R=2r-g-2; the halves each contain one one exactly when L,R<=r-1. An integer with that sum is attainable from the two capped intervals exactly when the sum is nonnegative and no greater than the sum of the caps. Resolving the minima yields the stated three upper bounds and the lower bound, including zero gaps and empty intervals. Two adjacent pairs give a union by half-length, not a sum; pure-zero classes are floor(M/2). Uniform indexed words correspond to uniform integer compositions. Their normalized gaps converge by simplex Riemann sums to the Dirichlet law; the rounded interval endpoints give uniform O(1/n) error in the normalized count, and the length of the union is continuous even at an interval's collapse. Boundedness gives first-moment convergence. Independent bounded replay enumerated active four-constraint systems by exact rational solves, triangulated hull boundaries (SciPy ConvexHull; only triangulation topology used floating point), and summed rational simplex determinants: 7 vertices and 12 boundary simplices for P1, 10 vertices and 26 for P12, volumes 1/32 and 13/864. This independently corroborates the original Ehrhart volumes without executing reproduce.py. In simplex coordinates the density is 6; it gives union contribution 41/144, while the simplex maximum gives H4/8=25/96, totaling 157/288. Both cited interior examples for the limit are consistent. The source's finite word checks are recorded evidence rather than an all-length proof.

value.rationale: This measures diversity in a natural, established equivalence, not a relabeling of literal diversity. The union resolves precisely which half-Parikh vectors are realized in the sparse regime; its nonconstant conditional law and exact mean quantify the scale-n effect and its nontrivial two-pair overlap, which the scale-n^2 literal-square law does not measure.
